correctness.rationale: The initial rank vector is bijective by successively inserting each new label into its prescribed position in the order of earlier labels. Its product weights give the required normalization, including the forced first record. In one-line order an ascent at i-1 is exactly R_(i-1)<R_i and a descent at i is exactly R_(i+1)<=R_i. With R_i=b<i their conditional probability is b(b-1)/[(theta+i-2)(theta+i)] since neither allowed choice reaches the earlier/new record rank; with b=i it is i/(theta+i). Summing b(b-1) gives i(i-1)(i-2)/3. In the numerator after subtracting 1/3, the i-dependent terms cancel: writing u=i-1, the product is (theta+u)^3-(theta+u); three times the summed numerator minus that product is -theta(theta-1)(theta-2). This also applies at i=2, when the nonrecord term vanishes. Positivity of the denominator gives the strict signs and two positive roots. Partial fractions of the shifted triple reciprocal telescope from theta to theta+n-3 and give the claimed expectation, with a strictly positive bracket for n>=3.
residual_risks: The proof concerns one-point marginals and their sum, not joint peak-set invariance or higher moments. The recorded permutation enumeration is finite corroboration only.

evidence: Bouvel–Nicaud–Pivoteau publishes the full rank construction and uses two ranks for one adjacent descent. Computing a peak additionally couples two inequalities through the center rank.

Gessel–Zhuang refine peaks by cycle type of the same permutation; turning a cycle count into a left-to-right record count by a change of permutation is not an identification of the corresponding one-line peak statistic. Billey–Burdzy–Sagan counts peak sets for uniform permutations.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The rank law is a strong algorithmic antecedent, but its stated descent calculation is not a stronger peak enumeration. Uniform and cycle-weighted peak laws do not cover the claimed record-weighted pair of adjacent comparisons.

evidence: The known rank law makes an efficient conditional computation possible; the record and nonrecord cases differ, and summing them before factoring produces the two exceptional positive biases.

value.rationale: A strict peak is a natural local refinement of the already studied descent statistic. Equality at the nonuniform bias theta=2 holds simultaneously at every interior position and finite size, with a sharp sign law on the three remaining open regimes. This is useful as an exact calibration and a distinction between a natural peak marginal and other local statistics under record bias; it is not inference about the complete distribution.
residual_risks: A narrow marginal invariant obtained by a short calculation; no higher-dimensional peak or asymptotic theory follows just from the equality.
